ops.title: ccx grep slowness: --ignore-files exonerated, auto-regex double walk is the real 2x
ops.body:
Measured 2026-07-27/28 on yasyf's machine while diagnosing "ccx code grep is pathologically slow quite frequently".

## The circulating diagnosis is wrong on both halves

A hypothesis in circulation blamed `ccx code grep --ignore-files` for `O(depth × rules)` gitignore parsing over dependency trees. Both halves are false:

**`--ignore-files` is not a ccx flag.** `ccx code grep` has no such flag and no ccx code path emits one. The engines are ripgrep, falling back to system grep (`internal/ripgrep/ripgrep.go:424-434` `resolveEngine`) — never ugrep. The only ignore-related flag ccx ever emits is a bare `--no-ignore-parent`, and only when `--scope` is set (`ripgrep.go:536-539`). The strings `ignore-files`/`ugrep` appear nowhere in the repo.

The flag comes from **Claude Code's own bundled-ugrep shell shim**: the `grep` function in the shell snapshot rewrites a bare `grep` to `ARGV0=ugrep <claude-bin> -G --ignore-files --hidden -I --exclude-dir=.git …`. So a raw `grep` in Bash is Claude Code's embedded ugrep, not ccx.

**`--ignore-files` is also nearly free — it usually pays for itself, because it prunes:**

| tree | with `--ignore-files` | without |
|---|---|---|
| Go module cache (5.6G, 237k files) | 24.8s | 26.0s |
| `~/.claude/plugins` (2.0G, 35k files) | 3.6s | 3.5s |
| cc-context repo (2.9G on disk) | 0.5s | 4.3s |

Cost tracks tree size, not ignore-rule depth.

## What actually costs

1. **Auto-regex escalation walks the whole tree twice.** A zero-match literal search whose pattern compiles as a regex re-runs the *full* search (`ripgrep.go:193-206`, and `runFilesWithMatches` `ripgrep.go:283-290`). Measured on the module cache: `zzzqqqnomatch` → 23.6s; `zzzqqq.*nomatch` → **41.3s at 109% CPU**. Agents search for `a|b` and `Foo.*Bar` constantly, so this fires often.
2. **No deadline on the engine subprocess.** `exec.CommandContext` (`internal/render/render.go:96-97`) gets only the SIGINT/SIGTERM context from `cmd/ccx/main.go:19`. Nothing bounds a runaway walk. The MCP server is long-lived — 15 `ccx mcp` processes were live — so concurrent dep-tree greps stack into sustained load.
3. **No repo-boundary check and no cost signal.** `internal/backend/pathcheck.go:42-72` accepts any path that stats. Dependency-tree awareness lives only in the capt-hook Python guards, which block *raw* `grep` (`search_common.py:186-220`) but deliberately sanction `ccx code grep --scope <dep path>` as the cc-context:dep-reader lane.

## Ruled out

- **Semantic index is healthy.** The cc-context index is 500 files, gitignore correctly honored — no `.claude/worktrees` (2.4G, 13 worktrees), no `.task`, no `target/`. Cold search 2.0s, warm 0.9s.
- **Index churn is not CPU.** 418 of 493 dirs under `~/Library/Caches/cc-context/semsearch` are 12K two-file test fixtures, not real index builds.

## Separate bug found

`internal/semsearch/index` tests write into the **real user cache**: 418 of 493 index dirs there are `dims:16` `auth.go`+`parse.go` fixtures, 768M total, ~200 new dirs on a busy day. `cache.Dir` (`internal/cache/cache.go:13-27`) already honors `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` before `os.UserCacheDir()` — the seam exists, the tests just don't use it. `cache.Dir` itself is correct.

## Reproduce

```sh
time ccx code grep "zzzqqqnomatch"   --scope ~/go/pkg/mod   # ~24s, single walk
time ccx code grep "zzzqqq.*nomatch" --scope ~/go/pkg/mod   # ~41s, double walk
```
